item.title: Irish Leaders Downplay Tensions as Trump Arrives For Visit
item.description: US President Donald Trump arrived in Ireland for a two-day visit, set for meetings with the country’s prime minister and president as well as plans to attend the Irish Open at his family’s golf resort.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Drug-Dealing Gangs Hold Key to Swedish Election in This Suburb
item.description: Salim Ali watched for years as young gang members openly dealt drugs in the square in front of his flower stall in the Stockholm suburb of Hässelby Gård.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Duxbury

item.title: Xi Takes Center Stage at Modi’s BRICS Summit as Iran War Deepens
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to kick off a BRICS summit in New Delhi that faces the difficult task of forging common ground, as the escalating war in the Middle East threatens fresh divisions.
item.dc:creator: Dan Strumpf, Sudhi Ranjan Sen and Josh Xiao

item.title: BRICS 2026 Summit New Delhi Live Updates: Modi, Putin, Xi Meet
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Arctic Summit Draws European Leaders as Russia Threat Grows
item.description: Finland’s prime minister, who convened the meeting, wants to see more funds directed to the region where Russia’s threat is growing
item.dc:creator: Kirsi Heikel and Alberto Nardelli

item.title: Kosovo Counts Down to War Crimes Trial of Former President Seen as Hero
item.description: Giant screens featuring digital timers appeared in squares and on main roads across Kosovo this month, counting down to Sept. 16 when judges in The Hague are due to deliver a verdict in the war crimes trial of former President Hashim Thaci.
item.dc:creator: Gresa Kraja

item.title: Lagarde Joins France Election Debate at Normandy Rally, Feeding ECB Exit Talk
item.description: Christine Lagarde will enter France’s presidential-election fray at a political gathering on Saturday, as speculation builds that she’ll leave the European Central Bank early.
item.dc:creator: William Horobin

item.title: Burnham’s Can-Do Attitude Put to Test as UK Budget Day Nears
item.description: When he entered 10 Downing St. Andy Burnham had a message for any cabinet minister or civil servant running up against a thorny policy problem: “No” is not good enough.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Trump Says Open to China Building Cars in US as Xi Visit Looms
item.description: President Donald Trump suggested he might be willing to allow a Chinese car company to build electric vehicles in the US if it did so with American workers, while pledging to maintain the effective US ban on imported vehicles from China.
item.dc:creator: Derek Wallbank and Amy Stillman

item.title: Oversight’s Comer Moves to Hold Leon Black in Contempt
item.description: The House Oversight Committee took a step toward holding billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress after he declined to comply with House subpoenas over his ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
item.dc:creator: Cam Kettles

item.title: North Korea Fires Multiple Short-Range Ballistic Missiles
item.description: North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles toward its east coast Saturday, a day after the US, South Korea and Japan wrapped up joint military exercises that Pyongyang views as a threat to its security.
item.dc:creator: Myungshin Cho

item.title: Remembering 9/11, 25 Years Later
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Ian Bremmer, President and Founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media, says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and the Houthis’ ability to threaten the Bab el-Mandeb Strait illustrate how weaker regional powers can gain leverage through disruption. Michael Duffey, Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, says that AI offers tremendous potential for the department, but says funding is essential to rebuilding the defense industrial base. Fred Wellman, Democratic Candidate for Missouri's Congressional 2nd District and a US military veteran of Iraq, says Missouri’s redistricting fight created confusion for voters and discusses his campaign’s effort to reach voters across the district following the court decision. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Ramps Up Controversial Probe of Trump’s Perceived Enemies
item.description: The US Justice Department is ramping up a controversial investigation into whether former government officials years ago conspired to undermine President Donald Trump, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm and Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Core CPI Hikes Ahead of FOMC Meeting
item.description: A key gauge of US consumer prices rose by more than expected last month, bolstering the case for Federal Reserve officials to raise interest rates next week. Bloomberg Intelligence US Interest Rate Strategist Ira Jersey and Bloomberg News Marco Strategist Frank Monkam discuss how the oil market is moving and what it all means for the Fed ahead of its September meeting next week. Then, Kalshi Chief Risk Officer Udesh Jha talks about the prediction market platform launch of Gold & Silver perpetual trading. Plus, the 2026 NFL season kicked off this week. Bloomberg News Senior Reporter and Co-Host of the 'Business of Sports' Podcast Randall Williams previews the season. All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wellman on Missouri Voters Face Redistricting Showdown
item.description: Fred Wellman, Democratic Candidate for Missouri's Congressional 2nd District and a US military veteran of Iraq, says his time as an Army reservist shaped his view of the burden of leadership as the country marks 25 years since 9/11. Wellman says Missouri’s redistricting fight created confusion for voters and discusses his campaign’s effort to reach voters across the district following the court decision. Wellman discusses his strategy for competing in the congressional race despite a significant fundraising gap with his opponent. He speaks with Tyler Kendall on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pentagon’s Top Weapons Buyer Says Congress Must Act on Munitions
item.description: A top Pentagon official said lawmakers must “step up and deliver” on the Trump administration’s $1.5 trillion funding request if the military is to replenish its stockpiles of key air defense interceptors and deep-strike weapons that have seen heavy use in the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Tyler Kendall

item.title: Merz Determined to Cling to Power and Defy Party Rebellion
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz is determined to hold on to power in Germany in defiance of the growing numbers within his party seeking to push him out of office, according to people familiar with his thinking.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs

item.title: Burnham’s EU Reset Under Pressure After Bloc’s Canada Deal
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was just weighing his first careful steps toward a reset with the European Union when he got lapped on the road to Brussels by Canada’s Mark Carney.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain, Alberto Nardelli, Ania Nussbaum and Alex Wickham

item.title: Russia’s Top IAEA Official Suspended Over Misogynist Screed
item.description: The top-ranked Russian official at the United Nations nuclear watchdog faces an ethics probe for writing a self-help book that described feminists as “hysterical fanatics” and gays and lesbians as “perverts” — and then promoting it to a UN youth group.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tirone

item.title: Iran Takes Defiant Stance as US War Deepens Its Isolation
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian gave a defiant speech after arriving in India for a BRICS summit marked by deep divisions as the war involving Iran, the US and Israel enters a dangerous new phase.
item.dc:creator: Dan Strumpf and Sudhi Ranjan Sen
